intended_object: The union ⋃_{i<k} H_i of the first k graphs of a family (H_i) of simple graphs on V: the graph whose edges are the edges of some H_i with i < k (from the docstring and the name).
explanation: In this definition, x and y are adjacent exactly when some i < k has them adjacent in H i. That is precisely the edge-union of H_0, …, H_{k-1}, and when k = 0 it gives the empty graph, as it should. Symmetry and the absence of loops are inherited from each H i. The section variables [Fintype V] and [DecidableEq V] are not used, so they are not hypotheses of the definition; it applies to any vertex type. Mathlib expresses the same object as the indexed supremum ⨆ i < k, H i in the complete lattice of simple graphs, and `SimpleGraph.iSup_adj` shows its adjacency is the same. The definition is therefore an equivalent re-implementation at the same generality, not a narrower one. The only restriction is V : Type instead of a universe-polymorphic type, which is incidental.
